subject: Post-call: NimHealth deployment paths and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: NimHealth deployment paths and next steps

Hi Sofia — great to speak earlier. Thanks for walking us through the NimHealth ingestion pattern and the PHI constraints. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so we stay aligned.

High-level requirements we heard:
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~1200 requests/min (peak: ~3000) with 1–2k token responses.
- Data classification: PHI (HIPAA scope) — must not leave customer VPC unless covered by BAAs and approved encryption/KMS.
- SLO targets: p99 inference latency target ~250–300ms, availability >= 99.9%.
- Isolation concern: primary ask is avoidance of noisy neighbor impact during peak batch processing.

Option framing (hosted vs dedicated vs private):
- Hosted API (fastest path): simplest and lowest friction. Works well if BAAs and regional isolation cover PHI — may require explicit contract and region pinning.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools (single-tenant) that address noisy neighbor and performance variability while still using Redwood control plane. Good for predictable throughput and cost predictability.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed network boundaries; best fit when data must be strictly isolated or when encryption/KMS needs to be fully controlled on customer side.

From our call, NimHealth preference looks to be private VPC or a dedicated VPC-enabled Dedicated deployment. Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll send a short scope worksheet (attached nim-reqs.xlsx) to capture expected QPS, model sizes, and token budget. Please fill and return by EOD Tue.
2) Technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (Rishi) to align on noisy-neighbor mitigations, NAT/EIP patterns, and KMS integration. Can you share a 90-min window next week?
3) We'll provide a Dedicated capacity price estimate + a Private deployment checklist and the Dedicated SLA (attached redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf).
4) If Private is the selected route, we’ll follow with deployment timelines and an on-prem/VPC decision matrix.

If that looks right, I’ll tee up the technical meeting and draft the mutual action plan in HubSpot.

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik — adding technical context you can forward to Sofia. TL;DR: three practical isolation approaches and what we would commit to from an SLO/operational perspective.

1) Hosted (multi-tenant) with hard isolation controls:
   - Network: region pinning + dedicated routing policies to minimize cross-tenant noisy traffic.
   - Guarantees: soft limits on noisy burst isolation, best-effort latency during extreme load (not recommended for strict PHI requirements).

2) Dedicated capacity (recommended middle ground):
   - Single-tenant GPU pools; tenants get exclusive nodes.
   - Autoscaling policy still under tenant control; we can reserve burst capacity for critical windows.
   - Operational commitments: separate monitoring/trace partitions, token-level cost isolation, and defined maintenance windows.
   - Typical p99 measurements: with Dedicated and continuous batching tuned for the workload, we routinely hit 150–300ms p99 for 1–2k token outputs on current A100-class nodes.

3) Private VPC / on-prem:
   - Full network and KMS control by customer; we provide a private control plane and on-prem packaging if needed.
   - For on-prem, dependencies and disk/local NVMe caches become customer-managed; we provide installers and runbooks.

Noisy-neighbor mitigations we’ll propose for Dedicated/Private:
- Preferrable: single-tenant node pools + submission-level QoS and reserved capacity windows.
- KV cache pinning: isolate large context users so hot KV entries don’t evict others.
- Batching policy per-tenant: predictable batch sizes during critical windows.

Attachments: I’m attaching the Dedicated SLA excerpt for legal to review (redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf). Happy to join the tech call — suggest Tue 2026-06-16 10:00–11:30 PT.

-rishi

Hi Karthik — thanks for the summary and Rishi, thanks for the technical notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Compliance: We will need a BAA and either a Private VPC or a Dedicated deployment with explicit contract language that prohibits cross-tenant data movement. Hosted multi-tenant is off the table unless there is a contractual isolation guarantee.
2) Timeline: NimHealth is aiming to run a pilot with 10 clinics by Sept 2026. Prefer start of POC by mid-July.
3) On-prem vs VPC: our security team prefers VPC-first (cloud-managed) for faster onboarding, but may request an on-prem option later for certain regions. Can you outline the incremental effort (days/weeks) to go from VPC to on-prem?
4) Pricing: can you share a ballpark committed monthly cost for Dedicated (baseline) and a one-time setup estimate for Private?

We’re available for the tech deep-dive Tue 16 Jun at 10:30 PT — can Rishi do 10:30–11:30? Also please include any contract/contact for BAAs.

Regards,
